questions.prompt: A prospect says her current system makes new clients set a password before they ever see a price. Which demo move answers this best?

options.text: Book a drop-in as a new client on a live site
Show the client profile created after a booking
Open the reports page and show new-client counts
Explain that passwords keep card details safe

questions.reveal: Let her see the difference. A live booking as a first-timer shows the one-page flow with no account step.

questions.prompt: A new client enters her details at checkout, then closes the page before paying. What happens?

options.text: Nothing is saved until the payment goes through
Her contact is captured as an abandoned checkout
The spot is held for her for the next 24 hours
She's charged once she reopens the booking link

questions.reveal: Momence creates the contact as soon as details go in, so the studio can follow up with someone who nearly booked.

questions.prompt: A member wants to bring her sister to class and pay for both. What do you show?

options.text: The sister makes her own account, then books
The desk books the sister through point of sale
A second spot in one checkout, with her details
A gift card the member sends so her sister can pay

questions.reveal: Reserving extra spots is built into checkout. The friend gets a contact record and her own booking email.

questions.prompt: A class fills every week, and the owner wants an open spot to go to whoever grabs it fastest. Which waitlist setup fits?

options.text: Offer the open spot to the first person in line
Raise the capacity once the waitlist is full
Let members overbook at the drop-in rate
Notify everyone; the first to claim it gets in

questions.reveal: The other mode offers the spot to the first person in line. Ask which the owner prefers, then set it up that way.

questions.prompt: An owner says instructors only find out who's new or injured after class. What do you show?

options.text: A pre-class email each instructor sends out
Roster flags for new, injured and milestones
The client list sorted by date they signed up
The intake form library for each class type

questions.reveal: Flags on the roster put that information in front of the instructor at check-in, with no extra work.

questions.prompt: Which ways can people be checked in to a class in Momence?

options.text: Only from the front desk computer in studio
Only by scanning a code in the branded app
Roster on a phone, or iPad self check-in
Automatically once the class start time passes

questions.reveal: Momence is mobile-first, so instructors can check people in from the room. An iPad up front handles self check-in.

questions.prompt: An owner asks how she'd tell everyone booked into tonight's class that it's starting 15 minutes late. What do you show?

options.text: A segment of that class, then a newsletter
A post on the studio's community page
The AI agent replying to whoever texts in
Contacting the class from the roster

questions.reveal: One click from the roster reaches everyone booked, by email, text or in-app. No list to build.

questions.prompt: A walk-in with no account turns up five minutes before class. What's the fastest way to get her in?

options.text: Add her from the roster and take payment in POS
Have her book on her phone, then check her in
Add her to the waitlist and charge her later
Turn her away until she's booked online first

questions.reveal: Staff add a walk-in straight from the class page and open point of sale with the class already in the cart.

questions.prompt: A pre-open studio is selling founding memberships months ahead. The owner worries about buyers who never show up. Which setting helps?

options.text: A usage limit that resets every billing period
Auto-refill once the client's last credit is used
An activation deadline so it starts on its own
A guest pass that expires after thirty days

questions.reveal: Activate on first use starts the membership at the first class. The deadline starts it anyway if the client never comes in.

questions.prompt: What does a price rule do?

options.text: Raises prices after a set number of visits
Adds a card fee to purchases by non-members
Sets the drop-in price shown at checkout
Gives clients with a set tag a lower price

questions.reveal: Members or a financial-assistance tag can get a lower price or a percentage off without asking for a code.

questions.prompt: A coach says, “My clients' packs should reload when the last session is used, not on a date.” What do you show?

options.text: Auto-refill that runs when credits run out
A monthly membership that renews on billing day
Staff adding credits by hand when they run low
A usage limit that resets every four weeks

questions.reveal: Packs can refill when credits run out, on a time interval, or whichever comes first.

questions.prompt: A wellness studio wants one membership with 10 classes and a separate allowance for sauna sessions. What's accurate?

options.text: A membership covers classes or appointments only
Classes and appointments get separate limits
Sauna sessions need a second membership on top
One limit applies, whatever the client books

questions.reveal: Usage limits can be set separately for classes and appointments, and you choose exactly what the membership covers.

questions.prompt: Clients at a stretch studio always want the same practitioner. How do you set up booking?

options.text: Let clients book any time, then assign staff later
Create a separate service for every practitioner
Use request-only booking so staff can confirm
Put the practitioner step before choosing a time

questions.reveal: Booking order is a setting. Practitioner first lets clients book their favorite; time first matches them to whoever is free.

questions.prompt: How can a studio hold an appointment without charging the client up front?

options.text: Save the card at booking, charge at the visit
Require full prepayment for every appointment
Send a payment link only after the session ends
Block clients who miss a session from booking

questions.reveal: A card on file reserves the spot. Staff take payment from the schedule when the client arrives.

questions.prompt: A client emails to cancel, then texts an hour later to keep her spot. The owner asks how she'd know which came last. What do you show?

options.text: The email inbox and the text log, side by side
Both messages in one thread, bookings beside it
A staff task created for each new message
The notes on the client's profile from last visit

questions.reveal: One thread per client across email, text, calls and in-app, with her memberships and visits in the side panel.

questions.prompt: A client calls the studio's Momence number and nobody picks up. What happens?

options.text: The call is passed to Momence support
The call drops and a text goes out instead
A transcribed voicemail lands in the inbox
The caller is sent to the studio's email

questions.reveal: Voicemails are transcribed, and staff can call back from Momence. The number can also forward to another line.

questions.prompt: An owner wants to invite her regulars to a new workshop without emailing her whole list. What do you show?

options.text: A newsletter to everyone with a members-only code
A segment by recent visit count, then a message
Each class roster, contacted one class at a time
A referral link shared by her top few clients

questions.reveal: Segments filter the client list by visits, purchases or tags. Then one message goes to just that group.

questions.prompt: An owner asks if her instructors will see total sales when they log in. What's accurate?

options.text: Everyone sees the same dashboard as the owner
Instructors see sales for their classes only
Instructors only get a schedule, no dashboard
Dashboards and permissions are set by role

questions.reveal: Each staff type gets its own permissions, and each person can customize their dashboard. Class profit is visible to admins only.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks, “Will Momence pay my instructors?” What's the accurate answer?

options.text: No. Reports show what's owed; pay is outside
Yes. Payroll is run and paid inside Momence
Yes, but only for instructors paid per class
No. Staff pay can't be tracked in Momence

questions.reveal: Pay rates and payroll reports show what each person is owed. The studio still pays staff outside Momence.

questions.prompt: Which is true of the free Momence app?

options.text: It lists nearby studios so clients find new ones
It costs the studio a fee for each download
Clients see only studios they're linked to
It's only included on the highest plan tier

questions.reveal: It isn't a marketplace. No other studio can advertise to the studio's clients there.
